mil5.1.10:0.4: 10. Question on the Display of Psychic Power
mil5.1.10:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this was spoken by the Blessed One:
mil5.1.10:1.2: ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed by the Tathāgata, made much of, made a vehicle, made a ground, established, consolidated, and well undertaken. If he wished, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could live for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.’
mil5.1.10:1.4: ‘At the end of three months from now the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.’
mil5.1.10:1.5: If, venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said,
mil5.1.10:1.6: ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed by the Tathāgata ... or for the remainder of an aeon,’ then the fixing of the limit at three months is false.
mil5.1.10:1.7: If, venerable sir, the Tathāgata said,
mil5.1.10:1.8: ‘At the end of three months from now the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna,’ then the statement ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed ... or for the remainder of an aeon’ is also false.
mil5.1.10:1.9: There is no roaring (empty boasting) by the Tathāgatas about what is impossible.
mil5.1.10:1.10: The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are of efficacious speech, of true speech, of speech without duplicity.
mil5.1.10:1.11: This double-pronged dilemma is profound, very subtle, and hard to understand; it has now come to you. Break this net of views, set it down on one side, and shatter the doctrines of opponents.”
mil5.1.10:2.1: “Your majesty, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed ... or for the remainder of an aeon,’ and the limit of three months was also stated. But that ‘aeon’ (kappa) is called the aeon of a life-span (āyukappa).
mil5.1.10:2.2: The Blessed One, your majesty, did not speak thus in proclaiming his own strength; rather, in declaring the power of psychic ability, the Blessed One spoke thus:
